p.scope-of-this-document: **Scope of this document.** This file defines *what* a campaign is, *which* artifact roles its paper trail carries, and the *canonical section skeleton* of a campaign plan — the one document that lets a large change be planned once and executed cold.

p.A-CAMPAIGN-IS-A-MULTI-COMMIT-CHANGE-TOO-: A campaign is a multi-commit change too big for one session: a package-family rename, a debt drain across the whole codebase, a new subsystem landed in six waves.

p.A-CAMPAIGN-IS-GATED-BY-PHASES-AND-PLANNE: It is executed as **gated phases** — each ends with the project's full gate panel green — and it is planned to run **cold**: by a fresh session with no memory of the planning conversation, by a different person, or by the author after total context loss.

p.THE-TEST-IS-WHETHER-A-STRANGER-COULD-EXE: The test of a good plan is not "could I execute this tomorrow?" but "could a stranger execute this today?".

p.PAY-THE-FORMATS-COST-ONLY-FOR-WORK-THAT-: The format's cost is real: pay it only when the work spans sessions or more than a handful of commits.

p.THE-CARRIER-CHOICE-LIVES-IN-FLOW-ADDRESS: What decides whether to pay this format's cost at all — or take another carrier for the work — is a choice with its own rule, and that rule lives in `flow:addressable-specs`'s `#what-goes-where`.

p.paper-trail-carries-five-roles-lead: A campaign's paper trail carries five roles:

td.fact: the frozen starting facts: gate-panel state, inventory counts, the numbers phases are measured against
falsifiable expectations, stated *before* execution so the report can honestly say confirmed / falsified / surprised
the running record: per-phase commit maps, deviations, discovered work
results vs predictions; what the campaign taught

p.THE-ONE-FILE-DIALECT-CARRIES-ALL-FIVE-RO: **The one-file dialect (default).** One plan document carries all five roles: the baseline in the target-arithmetic and current-state sections, the predictions in their own section, the log in the execution ledger, the report in the execution-record block prepended at close — one file, one resume pointer.

p.THE-ROLES-NOT-THE-COUNT-ARE-THE-CONTRACT: Very large campaigns may split the roles into files; the roles, not the count, are the contract.

facts.LAW-SKIPPING-THE-REPORT-LEARNS-NOTHING-D: **a campaign that skips the REPORT learns nothing durable,**
facts.LAW-NO-WRITTEN-PLAN-MEANS-NO-RESUMPTION: **and a campaign without a written PLAN cannot be resumed by anyone but its author's context window.**

p.WHICH-SECTIONS-ARE-WRITTEN-BEFORE-EXECUT: Sections 1 and 3–13 are written before execution; 2, 14, and 15 are filled by the executing session.

s1-status.title: 1 — Title and status line

p.the-title-and-the-status-block-lead: The title names the campaign and its one-line point; under it, an italic status block:

facts.STATUS-BLOCK-THE-TREE-THE-PLAN-WAS-WRITT: the tree the plan was written against,

p.OWNER-REVIEW-MAY-ANNOTATE-THE-STATE: Owner review may annotate the state (`ACCEPTED with owner amendments, <date>`) before execution.

s1-status.fence: # CACHE-DRAIN-PLAN v0.1 — retire the legacy cache, consumer by consumer _Status: PLANNED · written against tree `57fa42e` · cold-executable: any phase is a safe stop; the floor is green at every boundary._

p.at-close-a-block-is-prepended-lead: At close, the executing session prepends a block into the status area:

s3-mandate.title: 3 — The mandate

p.THE-MANDATE-IS-QUOTED-VERBATIM-AND-DATED: The owner's commissioning words, **quoted verbatim and dated** — never paraphrased into blandness.

p.SCOPE-QUESTIONS-RESOLVE-AGAINST-THE-MAND: Scope questions resolve against this text; the executor never re-litigates it.

s3-mandate.fence: Mandate (owner, 2026-07-07): "take everything listed in the previous campaign's deferral ledger and plan its implementation; do not wait for the full pilot — build a small demo project instead."

s4-arithmetic.title: 4 — Target arithmetic

p.BASELINE-AND-EXIT-STATE-ARE-EXACT-COUNTS: Baseline and exit state as **exact counts** that reconcile: every baseline unit ends in the exit state or in a phase that removes it.

p.VAGUE-TARGETS-MAKE-THE-REPORT-UNWRITABLE: Vague targets make the report unwritable.

s4-arithmetic.fence: Baseline at plan time: 130 findings = 68 message-format + 28 file-budget + 24 banned-call + 8 owner-gated + 2 one-shots. Exit state: 10 = 8 owner-gated (out of scope) + 2 parked (named). Everything else reaches zero.

p.FACTS-ARE-GATHERED-AT-AUTHORING-WITH-POI: Facts gathered at authoring, with file-and-line pointers, marked so the executor trusts them instead of re-investigating.

p.WRONG-FACTS-HERE-ARE-THE-MOST-EXPENSIVE-: **Wrong facts here are the most expensive class of plan bug: verify while writing.**

p.the-stale-trio-a-real-campaign-recorded: A real campaign recorded three files as stale at 566/556/554 lines; the true sizes were 609/612/608 — the author counted non-blank lines where the gate counts physical ones.

p.a-phase-zero-probe-caught-it: A Phase 0 probe caught what would have pruned live debt as stale.

s6-decisions.title: 6 — Decisions D1–DN

p.EACH-DECISION-WEIGHS-ITS-OPTIONS-AND-REA: Each weighs its options, marks the chosen one, and gives every rejection a reason — so a mid-execution surprise is resolved in the spirit of the plan, and nobody re-opens a settled question.

p.REJECTIONS-ARE-AS-LOAD-BEARING-AS-THE-CH: Rejections are as load-bearing as the choice.

s6-decisions.fence: ### D4 — how the shared engine reaches both consumers - (α) rewrite cross-package paths at install time — real product surface; rejected here, named as future work in the follow-up spec. - (β) align the two layouts — breaks a published invariant; rejected. - (γ) vendor-sync (CHOSEN): one authored home, byte-identical synced copies, a `--check` gate makes drift mechanically impossible.

p.PREDICTIONS-ARE-NUMBERED-FALSIFIABLE-AND: Numbered, falsifiable, stated before execution, checked one by one in the report — "P3 — fewer than 10 test expectations break across all 68 message edits: most tests match error kinds, not strings."

p.A-PREDICTION-THAT-CANNOT-FAIL-IS-A-HOPE: A prediction that cannot fail is a hope, not a prediction.

p.PHASE-ZERO-PRODUCES-NO-COMMITS-AND-LATER: Phase 0 is always spikes and probes and produces no commits; every later phase carries numbered steps, its own exit criterion, its own prediction, and its planned commit set with subjects spelled in advance.

p.A-PLAN-REFERENCES-FEATURE-DOCUMENTS-IT-D: **A plan references feature documents; it does not restate them.** Where a campaign executes work that has its own feature documents, the plan's phases and batches name those documents and stop there. The plan stays what it is — a statement of order, intent and acceptance — while each feature's own contract stays in one place with one author.

p.the-plan-is-the-copy-that-goes-stale: This is the general addressing law (`flow:addressable-specs`'s `##A-NORMATIVE-VALUE-LIVES-AT-EXACTLY-ONE-ANCHOR`) applied to this genre, and the echo names its anchor as that law requires. Restating a feature's substance inside the plan produces two statements of one truth with nothing forcing them to agree, and the plan is the copy that will go stale, because it is the one built to be thrown away.

p.EVERY-RISK-CARRIES-A-DETECTION-SIGNAL-AN: Named risks, each with its detection signal and its plan B — "flaky network: re-probe at each network-facing step; worst case those steps land red-pending-network, recorded, everything else lands."

p.A-RISK-WITHOUT-A-FALLBACK-IS-A-WISH: A risk without a fallback is a wish that nothing goes wrong.

p.NON-GOALS-ARE-NAMED-SO-THEY-STAY-VISIBLE: "What this plan deliberately does NOT do" — **named, so they stay visible.**

p.EVERY-NON-GOAL-CARRIES-A-REASON-AND-A-DI: Each non-goal carries a reason and a disposition: deferred to a named follow-up, held by the owner, or rejected outright — "does NOT extend the gate to the two remaining modules: that is the NEXT campaign's opening move, after this queue closes."

s11-quick-start.title: 11 — Quick-start for the executing session

p.the-quick-start-block-lead: The literal shell block a cold session runs first:

s11-quick-start.fence: git log --oneline -3 # tree must match the status line <gate-panel command> # full panel green before Phase 0 opens <baseline count command> # must print the §4 baseline figure

s12-acceptance.title: 12 — Whole-campaign acceptance

p.ACCEPTANCE-IS-A-RUNNABLE-SCRIPT-ASSERTIN: A runnable script asserting the end state — the campaign's definition of done, executed on a green floor at close, cited by the report.

s12-acceptance.fence: <gate-panel command>; echo "EXIT=$?" # exit 0 test ! -d src/legacy_cache # the drained module is gone <banned-pattern search> | wc -l # 0 references remain

p.REVIEW-POINTS-GO-OPEN-THEN-RESOLVED: Decisions only the owner can make, escalated as numbered points: `OPEN` with options and the executor's recommendation, later annotated `RESOLVED` with the ruling verbatim ([`phase-gates.md` §review-points](phase-gates.md#review-points)).

p.THE-LEDGER-BINDS-HASHES-TO-THE-PLANNED-S: Filled by the executing session: per-phase commit maps binding hashes to the planned subjects, with what each commit confirmed or falsified ([`execution-ledger.md`](execution-ledger.md)).

p.EVERY-DEFERRAL-IS-NAMED-WITH-AN-OWNER-AN: Everything the campaign chose not to do, named, one line each, with an owner and a disposition.

p.NOTHING-EVAPORATES: Nothing evaporates: leftover work is in a commit or in this ledger ([`execution-ledger.md` §deferrals](execution-ledger.md#deferrals)).

p.A-CLOSED-CAMPAIGNS-DEFERRALS-BECOME-THE-: A closed campaign's deferrals ledger **becomes the next campaign's mandate**: the owner commissions the follow-up by pointing at it, and the new plan's opening table maps each deferral to a closing phase.

p.CAMPAIGNS-FORM-A-CHAIN: Campaigns form a chain — no work item is lost between links, and no campaign starts blank ([`execution-ledger.md` §lineage](execution-ledger.md#lineage)).

temporary.title: A plan is a temporary artifact

p.A-PLAN-MUST-BE-DELETABLE-WHEN-EXECUTED: A campaign plan is **temporary by design**. When it has been executed it must be possible to delete it and have nothing break. If deleting a finished plan breaks something, that something was depending on scaffolding.

p.THE-TEST-IS-DELETION-NOT-TIDINESS: The test is deletion, and it is worth stating as a test rather than as a preference: a project cannot tell, by looking, whether its plans are load-bearing. Asking "could this file be removed today?" answers it in one question, and answers it the same way for every plan.

p.SIGNIFICANT-CONTENT-MOVES-INTO-THE-SPECS: Significant content — a rule the campaign established, a decision with its reasons, a measurement that will be re-read — moves **into the specifications** as the item closes. What stays in the plan is the record of doing, which git already keeps.

p.TOMBSTONES-ARE-PROCESS-SUPPORT-NOT-STRUC: A **tombstone** — the one-line trace a closed row leaves in the plan — is process support for whoever is walking the plan, and nothing more. It is not part of the project's structure, nothing may cite it, and it goes when the plan goes.

p.WHY-DISPOSABLE-ZONES-KEEP-DURABLE-FINDIN: The failure this prevents has a shape worth recognising: a correct, carefully-argued finding written into a campaign document, which behaves exactly as the zone promises — it is disposable, so it is disposed of, and the finding is rediscovered months later at full cost. The zone was not wrong; filing something durable there was.

p.THE-ADDRESSING-HALF-LIVES-IN-ADDRESSABLE: The other half of this rule — that a statement cites the spec element and never the plan row, and that re-pointing citations is part of closing — belongs to the addressable-specs flow, at `spec://org.vibevm.world/addressable-specs/flows/addressable-specs/ADDRESSABLE-SPECS-PROTOCOL#disposable-targets`. One law, two homes, one pointer.

re-derive.title: Re-derive for your project

p.re-derive-lead: Run this prompt once to adapt the format to a concrete project:

re-derive.fence: Read CAMPAIGN-PLAN-FORMAT.md, phase-gates.md, and execution-ledger.md. Adapt the campaign-plan format to this project: 1. Name the gate panel: the exact commands that define this project's green floor, and how long a full run takes. 2. Name where campaign plans live (a version-controlled directory) and the filename convention (<NAME>-PLAN-v<N>.md). 3. Name the owner: who commissions campaigns and rules review points. 4. Write the quick-start block a fresh session runs before Phase 0. 5. Draft the whole-campaign acceptance skeleton: the script shape that asserts an end state in this project's tooling. 6. Record the adapted conventions in the project's boot documents so every future session loads them. Do not start a campaign; produce the adapted conventions only.

facts.SUM-A-CAMPAIGN-IS-GATED-PHASES-PLANNED-T: A campaign is a multi-commit change executed as gated phases, planned to run cold — by a stranger, today.
facts.SUM-FIVE-ROLES-ONE-FILE-BY-DEFAULT: Five roles: PLAN, BASELINE, PREDICTIONS, LOG, REPORT — one file by default. Skip the report and the campaign learns nothing durable.
facts.SUM-THE-DEFERRALS-LEDGER-SEEDS-THE-NEXT-: The deferrals ledger seeds the next campaign's mandate.
